fragments.text: one of your agents ran a repro that crashed agency

reply_text:
㊥ (apology) I'm sorry. That was most likely claude-8, in the investigation I sent it of the `id()`-keyed tables. Agency is answering again and the three jobs I'd dispatched are still making progress, but I can't yet say which process brought it down. I've made the memory cap a standing rule in every packet's instructions.

㊢ ("ran a repro that crashed agency") claude-8 ran three small reproduction scripts (`repro_t1.py`, `repro_t5.py`, `probe_free.py`) between 16:19 and 16:20, the minute before Agency restarted at 16:20:50. My retry packet told it to run them under a 4 GB cap, and I haven't confirmed that it did. Its first attempt, at 11:41, ran a script that parses all of `Init.Prelude` and `Init.Notation`, and that job was SIGKILLed. That could also explain the four hours this morning when nothing reached me, but I haven't confirmed that either. One other process in the same minute had no cap: a pytest run by codex-19. claude-8's job has now finished, so nothing of its is still running.

㊢ (state after the restart) Agency is answering. The structterm2, preludedump and clean1 jobs have each recorded new events since the restart. Two of my parks survived; I haven't checked whether others were lost.

🈲 (rule from now on) Every packet's instructions now require any Python process that loads the port to run under `systemd-run` with a memory cap: probes, pytest, traces and reproductions. Without the cap, the process runs inside Agency's own memory allowance, and when it grows it takes Agency and every agent's job with it.

㊢ (what claude-8 found) The report is useful. 5 tables can lose their keys while still holding them, and 3 are unclear. One stale lookup was actually reproduced, in `generated_origins_by_id`: an object is freed, its address is reused, and the lookup returns the old object's origin, in 3 of 3 runs. That table gets its own fix packet, which will require the memory cap.

previous_reply_acts.text: ("compiles-correct is no longer the ideal measure") Agreed. By the comparator's measure, no row is finished yet. Even the two cleanest rows in the audit match only a few of Lean's term nodes: `mkListNode` matched 3, and Lean has 7 more that the port's capture has nothing for. Those 7 include the signature types and the recursive self-reference.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text:
("rebuild them") Once `mkListNode` is clean, I'll rebuild every row cold, once, with the comparator. Each row's first finding then becomes the list of what to fix next, and the progress page will count clean rows instead of compiles-correct. Two things have to be in place first:
- **Lean dumps for `Init.Prelude`:** the dump tool can't load it yet, so 7 rows have no Lean dump.
- **Structure-instance terms:** structterm comes back, because `{ s with … }` is the most common gap.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text: (meanwhile) withRef and atEnd carry on: they still stop the port before the comparator has anything to compare. I'm parked on codex-23's checkpoint as `park-0772dd53`.
